pharm: Broad-spectrum bactericidal fluoroquinolone that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication; approved for veterinary use only.

summary: Enrofloxacin is a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibacterial approved for VETERINARY use only (e.g., Baytril) - it is NOT approved for and should NOT be used in humans. It is used in dogs and cats (and other species) to treat susceptible bacterial infections of the skin, respiratory tract, urinary tract and other sites. In dogs it is typically dosed 5-20 mg/kg by mouth once daily; in cats the dose must NOT exceed 5 mg/kg/day because higher doses can cause acute, sometimes irreversible, retinal toxicity and blindness. Like other fluoroquinolones it inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. Veterinary precautions include avoiding use in immature/growing animals (cartilage damage in weight-bearing joints) and in animals with seizure disorders (lowered seizure threshold), and avoiding co-administration with cation-containing products that impair absorption. It is partly metabolized to ciprofloxacin in animals.
indications: VETERINARY: management of bacterial infections in dogs and cats caused by enrofloxacin-susceptible organisms (e.g., skin and soft tissue infections, respiratory tract infections, urinary tract infections)
VETERINARY: used in various other animal species per approved labels; NOT indicated for humans

dosage.d: 5-20 mg/kg by mouth once daily (or divided every 12 hours), based on infection severity and organism susceptibility
Must NOT exceed 5 mg/kg per day (single daily dose) due to risk of retinal toxicity/blindness
dosage.n: Strict ceiling of 5 mg/kg/day in cats

dosage.d: Not approved or recommended for human use at any dose

admin: VETERINARY product - administer to animals only, exactly as directed by a veterinarian
Give oral tablets with or without food; separate from products containing aluminum, magnesium, calcium, iron or zinc (e.g., antacids, sucralfate, dairy) which reduce absorption
Do not exceed 5 mg/kg/day in cats because of the risk of retinal damage and blindness
Avoid use in young, growing animals (risk of cartilage/joint damage) unless the benefit outweighs the risk
Not for human administration; keep out of reach of children and humans
moa: Enrofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone that exerts a bactericidal effect by inhibiting bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, enzymes required for supercoiling and separation of bacterial DNA during replication and transcription. Inhibition of these enzymes prevents DNA synthesis and leads to bacterial cell death. It has a broad spectrum against many Gram-negative and some Gram-positive organisms. In animals it is partially metabolized to ciprofloxacin, an active fluoroquinolone metabolite.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to enrofloxacin or other quinolones/fluoroquinolones (in the treated animal)
relative: Immature/growing animals (cartilage erosions and arthropathy in weight-bearing joints)
Animals with known or suspected seizure disorders (fluoroquinolones may lower seizure threshold)
Cats at doses above 5 mg/kg/day (retinal toxicity)
Pregnant or nursing animals unless clearly warranted
monitor: Cats: vision and signs of retinal change (dilated pupils, blindness)

preg: Not for human use. In veterinary practice, enrofloxacin is generally avoided in pregnant animals unless the severity of infection warrants treatment, because fluoroquinolones may affect developing cartilage.
lact: Not for human use. In veterinary practice it is generally avoided in nursing animals where possible, as fluoroquinolones may pass into milk and affect developing offspring.
renal: Not a human medication. In animals with renal impairment, the dose may be reduced and dosing interval extended by the veterinarian, since fluoroquinolones are partly renally eliminated.
hepatic: Not a human medication. In animals, enrofloxacin is partly metabolized in the liver (including to ciprofloxacin); use cautiously in hepatic impairment under veterinary guidance.

major: Theophylline (in animals) - fluoroquinolones can raise theophylline levels and risk toxicity
Other seizure-threshold-lowering drugs - additive CNS excitation
moderate: Cation-containing products (antacids, sucralfate, iron, calcium, zinc, dairy) - chelation reduces enrofloxacin absorption; separate administration
Nephrotoxic or other antibacterials - veterinary judgment required
minor: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (in animals) - potential additive CNS stimulation reported with some fluoroquinolones
interactions.food: Reduced absorption with calcium-rich foods (e.g., dairy) and cation-containing supplements; separate dosing.
interactions.diagnostics: Not applicable to human laboratory testing.

common: Gastrointestinal upset in animals (vomiting, decreased appetite, diarrhea)
serious: Retinal degeneration and blindness in cats (dose-related)
emergency: Acute blindness in cats (urgent veterinary attention)

monitoring: Cats: monitor vision and watch for dilated pupils or sudden blindness; do not exceed 5 mg/kg/day
Young animals: monitor for lameness or joint problems
Watch for neurologic signs or seizures
Monitor clinical response to therapy and gastrointestinal tolerance
counsel: This is a VETERINARY antibiotic for animals only and is NOT for human use - do not take it yourself or give it to people
Give it to your pet exactly as your veterinarian directs and complete the full course
In cats, never exceed the dose your vet prescribed - too much can cause permanent blindness; report any vision changes immediately
Separate the dose from antacids, dairy, or supplements containing calcium, iron, magnesium or zinc, which reduce its effect
Tell your vet if your pet has seizures or is young/growing; report vomiting, loss of appetite, lameness, or unusual behavior
pk: Bactericidal activity begins soon after absorption (within hours) in animals
Peak plasma levels generally within 1-3 hours of oral dosing in animals
Store at controlled room temperature per the veterinary product label; keep out of reach of children
pearls: VETERINARY fluoroquinolone, NOT for human use - do not administer to people under any circumstances
In CATS the dose must not exceed 5 mg/kg/day; higher doses cause acute, often irreversible retinal degeneration and blindness
Avoid in immature/growing animals (cartilage/joint damage) and in animals with seizure disorders
Cation-containing products (antacids, dairy, iron, calcium, zinc) chelate the drug and reduce absorption - separate dosing
Partly metabolized to ciprofloxacin in animals
missed: Not applicable to humans. For treated animals, the veterinary instruction is to give a missed dose as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, in which case the missed dose is skipped and the regular schedule resumed - never double up.
overdose: Not applicable to humans (not a human drug). In animals, overdose may cause vomiting, anorexia, CNS excitation or seizures, and, in cats, acute retinal toxicity/blindness. There is no specific antidote; veterinary management is supportive (discontinue the drug, control seizures, provide supportive care).
